items.title: Anomaly-Based Real Estate Trading Strategies Backtest Study
items.source_summary: Quantpedia study examines trend-following (moving average) and momentum strategies on real estate sector (RlEst index) using 99 years of Fama-French data (July 1926–Dec 2025), measuring risk-adjusted returns vs. sector and broader market benchmarks.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's backcheck-score.py lacks sector-specific accuracy calibration. Real estate sector exhibits distinct seasonality, leverage cycles, and rate sensitivity that generic backtesting cannot capture. The study's 99-year horizon and monthly granularity reveal SOFAR's missing time-of-month and sector-cycle weighting in vol-regime.py. Additionally, trend-following and momentum signal decay is not tier-separated by real estate supply/demand fundamentals vs. macro rate regime.

proposed_change.change_description: Add sector-specific regime accuracy tracking to backcheck-score.py (separate RlEst from broad market). Extend vol-regime.py to weight seasonal tendencies in real estate (Q4 year-end transactions, spring/summer supply peaks, rate-cycle correlation). Add a 'sector_accuracy_by_regime' field to track strategy Sharpe ratio by rate environment (rising/falling/stable). For trend/momentum decay, add time-of-month weighting in gex-calculator.py for large real estate hedges (SPY puts vs REIT calls).

items.evidence_basis: Quantpedia publishes rigorous academic backtests with transparent data (Fama-French public library), 99-year sample size reduces overfitting risk, and monthly frequency is standard for institutional rebalance. However, the source title only hints at results; full performance metrics, Sharpe ratios, and regime breakdowns not provided in excerpt.
items.credibility_basis: Quantpedia is peer-reviewed, uses public Fama-French data, methodology is reproducible, 99-year historical span reduces luck bias
items.author: Quantpedia
